purpose: Telavancin is a strong antibiotic used to treat serious skin infections and certain dangerous lung infections caused by bacteria. It is typically used in a hospital setting when other antibiotics may not work well. It is especially useful against a tough bacteria called MRSA (methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus).
how_it_works: Telavancin works by attacking the outer wall of harmful bacteria in two different ways at the same time, which makes it very effective. Think of it like a double lock on a door — it blocks bacteria from building their protective wall AND disrupts their ability to hold themselves together. This causes the bacteria to fall apart and die, stopping the infection.
common_side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, foamy urine, changes in taste (a metallic or soapy taste in your mouth), headache, dizziness, and redness or flushing of the face and neck during the infusion. You may also notice your urine looks unusual or foamy.
warnings: This medication can harm your kidneys, so your kidney function will be closely monitored with blood tests during treatment. It should NOT be used during pregnancy as it can cause serious harm to an unborn baby — reliable birth control is required. It may also affect your heart rhythm, so tell your doctor if you have any heart conditions. It can interact with other medications, so always tell your healthcare team everything you are taking.
typical_dosing: Telavancin is given through an IV (a drip into your vein) in a hospital or clinic setting — you will not take this as a pill at home. The usual dose is 10 mg per kilogram of your body weight, given once every 24 hours. Each dose is infused slowly over 60 minutes. Your doctor will adjust the dose if you have kidney problems. Treatment usually lasts 7 to 21 days depending on your infection.
